data.narrative:
Westmag is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Hansen and Jordan Sanders that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though the private peer set in this sector includes names such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation lever. Using total capital raised ($11M) as a proxy for seed-stage enterprise value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier—the typical progression multiple from seed to Series A—yields an implied valuation of $28M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied; while ten robotics peers exist broadly in the dataset, the tight filters required (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) yielded fewer than three datapoints necessary for robust comparison.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $23M to $32M, with a median point of $28M. This range reflects the single-method foundation and inherent stage-specific uncertainty. Key uncertainties include capital deployment efficiency and product-market progression metrics not detailed in the supplied data, as well as the limited peer-level visibility within the narrow robotics frontier-tech category. Further substantiation would require revenue traction, burn metrics, or comparable transaction multiples within the robotics sector.
